sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for Dealbook, a daily newsletter at The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《Dealbook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举行的Dealbook峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最有影响力的领导人，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zilron Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the Dealbook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔隆·蒙达尼等许多人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以观看其中一些毫无防备、未经修饰的对话实况。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch, free, at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在nytimes.com上直播部分采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅用户，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得我们所有新闻内容一个月的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》节目。

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 今天。

sentences.en: In a joint statement signed by President Trump and Kim Jong-un,
sentences.zh: 在特朗普总统和金正恩签署的一份联合声明中，

sentences.en: North Korea committed to complete denuclearization.
sentences.zh: 朝鲜承诺实现完全无核化。

sentences.en: Why is a promise that big being dismissed as meaningless?
sentences.zh: 为什么这样一个重大的承诺却被视为毫无意义？

sentences.en: It's Wednesday, June 13th.
sentences.zh: 今天是6月13日，星期三。

sentences.en: The letter that we're signing is very comprehensive, and I think both sides are going to be very impressed with the result.
sentences.zh: 我们签署的这份文件非常全面，我认为双方都会对结果印象深刻。

sentences.en: A lot of goodwill went into this.
sentences.zh: 这其中倾注了大量的善意。

sentences.en: A lot of work.
sentences.zh: 大量的工作。

sentences.en: A lot of preparation.
sentences.zh: 大量的准备。

sentences.en: I want to thank everybody on both sides, Secretary Pompeo and all of his counterparts.
sentences.zh: 我要感谢双方的所有人，感谢蓬佩奥国务卿和他的所有同行。

sentences.en: They were absolutely fantastic.
sentences.zh: 他们表现得非常出色。

sentences.en: And I would actually say that it worked out for both of us far better than anybody could have expected.
sentences.zh: 我甚至想说，这对我们双方来说，结果都比任何人预期的要好得多。

sentences.en: I think far better.
sentences.zh: 我认为好得多。

sentences.en: I watched the various news reports.
sentences.zh: 我看了各种新闻报道。

sentences.en: I would say far better than anybody even predicted.
sentences.zh: 我想说，这比任何人的预测都要好得多。

sentences.en: And this is going to lead to more and more and more.
sentences.zh: 而且这将带来更多、更多、更多的成果。

sentences.en: And it's an honor to be with you.
sentences.zh: 能与你在一起是我的荣幸。

sentences.en: Very great honor.
sentences.zh: 非常大的荣幸。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Thank you to all of your representatives very much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你们所有的代表。

sentences.en: Mr. Kim, would you like to come to Washington?
sentences.zh: 金先生，您愿意来华盛顿吗？

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Thank you, everybody.
sentences.zh: 谢谢大家。

sentences.en: So, Nick, what are you thinking as this deal is being struck between the president of the United States and the leader of North Korea?
sentences.zh: 那么，尼克，当美国总统和朝鲜领导人达成这项协议时，你在想什么？

sentences.en: What's your initial read on it?
sentences.zh: 你最初的解读是什么？

sentences.en: Well, I think our president got hoodwinked.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为我们的总统被忽悠了。

sentences.en: Nick Kristof is a columnist for The Times.
sentences.zh: 尼克·克里斯托夫是《纽约时报》的专栏作家。

sentences.en: I mean, it's not really a deal.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这根本算不上什么协议。

sentences.en: It's a piece of paper that aspires to a deal.
sentences.zh: 这只是一张渴望达成协议的纸。

sentences.en: But it looks like we gave up a fair amount just to get that piece of paper.
sentences.zh: 但看起来我们为了得到这张纸，放弃了相当多的东西。

sentences.en: And North Korea didn't really supply anything.
sentences.zh: 而朝鲜并没有真正提供任何东西。

sentences.en: And why do you say that?
sentences.zh: 你为什么这么说？

sentences.en: What did both sides agree to?
sentences.zh: 双方都同意了什么？

sentences.en: What did they really give up?
sentences.zh: 他们到底放弃了什么？

sentences.en: Chairman Kim and I just signed a joint statement in which he reaffirmed his unwavering commitment to complete denuclearization of the Korean peninsula.
sentences.zh: 金委员长和我刚刚签署了一份联合声明，他在声明中重申了对朝鲜半岛完全无核化的坚定承诺。

sentences.en: North Korea reaffirmed its commitment to denuclearize the Korean peninsula.
sentences.zh: 朝鲜重申了其实现朝鲜半岛无核化的承诺。

sentences.en: Chairman Kim has told me that North Korea is already destroying a major missile engine testing site.
sentences.zh: 金委员长告诉我，朝鲜已经在摧毁一个主要的导弹发动机试验场。

sentences.en: The U.S.
sentences.zh: 美国

sentences.en: provided security guarantees to North Korea.
sentences.zh: 向朝鲜提供了安全保障。

sentences.en: We will be stopping the war games, which will save us a tremendous amount of money.
sentences.zh: 我们将停止战争游戏，这将为我们节省一大笔钱。

sentences.en: And also to halt what President Trump called war games, essentially military exercises in the area.
sentences.zh: 同时还要停止特朗普总统所说的战争游戏，也就是该地区的军事演习。

sentences.en: So under the circumstances that we're negotiating a very comprehensive, complete deal, I think it's inappropriate to be having war games.
sentences.zh: 所以，在我们要谈判达成一项非常全面、完整的协议的情况下，我认为进行战争游戏是不合适的。

sentences.en: So why in your mind does that represent the U.S.
sentences.zh: 那么在你看来，为什么这代表美国

sentences.en: giving up a lot and not getting much in return?
sentences.zh: 放弃了很多却没得到什么回报？

sentences.en: Because to my mind, on the surface, denuclearization seems like the highest possible aim of these negotiations.
sentences.zh: 因为在我看来，从表面上看，无核化似乎是这些谈判中最高的目标。

sentences.en: And something like military exercises, the U.S.
sentences.zh: 而像军事演习，也就是美国

sentences.en: and South Korea basically doing war games, seems kind of symbolic and maybe even meaningless.
sentences.zh: 和韩国进行的那些战争游戏，看起来有点象征意义，甚至可能毫无意义。

sentences.en: They're essentially kind of theater.
sentences.zh: 它们本质上是一种表演。

sentences.en: So it seems like the U.S.
sentences.zh: 所以看起来美国

sentences.en: is giving up something kind of small and getting something seemingly huge.
sentences.zh: 放弃了一些微不足道的东西，却得到了看似巨大的东西。

sentences.en: It's actually kind of the reverse.
sentences.zh: 实际上恰恰相反。

sentences.en: We're really not getting something huge.
sentences.zh: 我们并没有真正得到什么巨大的东西。

sentences.en: And let me explain the background of the word denuclearization.
sentences.zh: 让我来解释一下“无核化”这个词的背景。

sentences.en: Which is a seemingly huge thing we're getting.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们得到的看似巨大的东西。

sentences.en: Which is the big thing that supposedly they're giving.
sentences.zh: 也就是他们理应放弃的那个大东西。

sentences.en: This goes back to 1992 when we were negotiating nuclear disarmament.
sentences.zh: 这要追溯到1992年，当时我们正在谈判核裁军。

sentences.en: And North Korea didn't want to disarm.
sentences.zh: 朝鲜不想裁军。

sentences.en: And so we came up with the word denuclearize to create some fudge room.
sentences.zh: 所以我们想出了“无核化”这个词来创造一些回旋余地。

sentences.en: And to—
sentences.zh: 为了——

sentences.en: Fudge room for who?
sentences.zh: 谁的回旋余地？

sentences.en: Basically for North Korea.
sentences.zh: 基本上是为朝鲜。

sentences.en: So when North Korea uses the word denuclearization, they don't mean that they hand over nuclear weapons, except maybe in some distant paradise far off.
sentences.zh: 所以当朝鲜使用“无核化”这个词时，他们并不意味着要交出核武器，除非是在遥远的未来某个遥不可及的天堂里。

sentences.en: To North Korea, it means that South Korea will not be protected by American nuclear weapons.
sentences.zh: 对朝鲜来说，这意味着韩国将不再受到美国核武器的保护。

sentences.en: So in other words, that the U.S.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，就是美国

sentences.en: and South Korea are no longer in an alliance.
sentences.zh: 和韩国不再是盟友关系。

sentences.en: And so it's very easy for North Korea to make these commitments about denuclearization because it's essentially saying, okay, you guys act firSt.
sentences.zh: 所以朝鲜做出这些关于无核化的承诺非常容易，因为它本质上是在说，好吧，你们先采取行动。

sentences.en: And then down the road at some point, we won't need nuclear weapons and the problem will be solved.
sentences.zh: 然后未来某个时候，我们就不需要核武器了，问题也就解决了。

sentences.en: But why would the U.S.
sentences.zh: 但如果正如你所说，这个词似乎并不意味着我们大家所认为的意思，即它实际上意味着美国

sentences.en: agree to use this word if, as you say, that word doesn't seem to mean what we all think it means, that it really means for the U.S.
sentences.zh: 要放弃对南方的核保护，以及朝鲜或许要放弃自己的一些核武器，那么美国为什么要同意使用这个词呢？

sentences.en: to give up a nuclear protection of the South, as well as the North perhaps giving up some nuclear weapons of its own?
sentences.zh: 所以从历史上看，美国

sentences.en: So historically, the U.S.
sentences.zh: 同意使用“无核化”是因为我们知道我们无法达成裁军协议。

sentences.en: has agreed to denuclearization because we know that we can't get a deal and disarmament.
sentences.zh: 朝鲜永远不会同意。

sentences.en: North Korea will never agree to it.
sentences.zh: 所以我们接受这种模糊性，因为至少它是达成协议的基础，

sentences.en: And so we accept this ambiguity because at least it's the basis for an agreement,
sentences.zh: 即使它在以后很难实施，因为它对朝鲜和对我们来说意义不同。

sentences.en: even if it is really difficult to implement later on because it means different things to North Korea than it is to us.
sentences.zh: 听起来你是在说，美国方面有一种“心知肚明的无知”，

sentences.en: It sounds like you're saying there's kind of a knowing ignorance on the part of the U.S.
sentences.zh: 即朝鲜同意使用“无核化”这个词，绝不意味着他们会立即销毁核武器。

sentences.en: here that North Korea is agreeing to a word, denuclearization, that in no way really means they will get rid of their nuclear weapons right away.
sentences.zh: 但也许有一天他们会这样做。

sentences.en: But maybe someday they'll do it.
sentences.zh: 而大家的共识是，我们通过谈判讨论一个模糊的词，总比让朝鲜用核战争威胁我们要好。

sentences.en: And the understanding is that it's better for us to be talking about a word that's ambiguous and negotiating than having North Korea threatening us with nuclear war.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's right.
sentences.zh: 坦率地说，我认为更重要的一点是，无核化是他们过去多次向我们兜售的东西，

sentences.en: And frankly, I mean, I think that the bigger point is that denuclearization is something they've sold us many times in the past,
sentences.zh: 而且往往比这次更具体地说明了将如何实现。

sentences.en: often with much greater specificity about how it would be done than this time.
sentences.zh: 所以，在这次峰会上，一个本来就模糊不清的词被以一种特别模糊和含混的形式使用了。

sentences.en: So an already ambiguous kind of fuzzy word was used in an especially ambiguous and fuzzy form in this summit.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们被忽悠了，赞美朝鲜半岛无核化只是一个漂亮的公关姿态。

sentences.en: I think we got bamboozled and that it's a nice public relations gesture to hail the denuclearization of the Korean Peninsula.
sentences.zh: 但这从1992年起就一直被赞美。

sentences.en: But this has been hailed all the way back since 1992.
sentences.zh: 从来没产生过任何实际意义。

sentences.en: Hasn't ever meant anything.
sentences.zh: 没有理由认为它在2018年会比1992年更有意义。

sentences.en: And there's no reason to think that it will be any more meaningful in 2018 than it was in 1992.
sentences.zh: 那么，尼克，为什么美国在这些谈判中放弃的东西如此重要？

sentences.en: So, Nick, why is what the United States gave up in these negotiations such a big deal?
sentences.zh: 嗯，这些军事演习，我们一年中会进行一系列演习，既有大型的也有小型的。

sentences.en: Well, so these military exercises, we hold a series of them around the year, both big ones and small ones.
sentences.zh: 大型演习可能涉及数十万军队。

sentences.en: The big ones can involve hundreds of thousands of troops.
sentences.zh: 待命。

sentences.en: Stand by.
sentences.zh: 接触。

sentences.en: Contact.
sentences.zh: 它们涉及模拟战斗，练习为应对任何形式的朝鲜攻击做好准备。

sentences.en: They involve, you know, simulated battles, practicing to be ready for any kind of North Korean attack.
sentences.zh: 现在，把它们想象成一次大型消防演习。

sentences.en: Now, think of them as a big fire drill.
sentences.zh: 如果你不定期进行消防演习，一旦发生火灾，你就无法做好准备。

sentences.en: And if you don't have fire drills periodically, you're not going to be ready if there is a fire.
sentences.zh: 所以它们一直被视为军事战备的核心，也是我们与韩国和日本关系的关键部分。

sentences.en: And so they've always been regarded as essential to military readiness and also as a crucial part of our relationship with South Korea and with Japan.
sentences.zh: 而且我们不仅停止了军事演习，在这样做的时候还没有咨询我们的盟友。

sentences.en: And not only did we halt military exercises, but we didn't consult our allies in doing so.
sentences.zh: 所以美国在与金正恩谈判期间，并没有就特朗普总统的这一决定与韩国商量，即我们不再进行这些演习了。

sentences.en: So the United States did not talk to South Korea about this decision by President Trump in the middle of negotiations with Kim Jong-un to say we're not going to be doing these exercises anymore.
sentences.zh: 通常情况下，峰会是经过高度规划的。

sentences.en: Normally, summits are highly planned.
sentences.zh: 所以你会提前与盟友协商。

sentences.en: And so you would consult with your allies ahead of time.
sentences.zh: 韩国似乎对取消演习完全感到意外。

sentences.en: South Korea seems to have been completely taken by surprise by the cancellation of exercises.
sentences.zh: 五角大楼似乎也感到意外。

sentences.en: The Pentagon seems also to have been taken by surprise.
sentences.zh: 所以这次谈判中我们最大的盟友韩国，以及我们自己的军方，都没有预料到这一点。

sentences.en: So this was not anticipated by either our biggest ally in this negotiation, South Korea, or our own military.
sentences.zh: 目前看来确实如此。

sentences.en: At the moment, that's what seems to be the case.
sentences.zh: 所以你认为，在许多人看来结束韩国军事演习是一件小事，但实际上可能是一件大事。

sentences.en: So in your mind, what to many of us looks like a small deal ending these military exercises in South Korea is perhaps a very big deal.
sentences.zh: 而表面上看起来是一件大事，即朝鲜说要无核化，实际上是一件相当小的事。

sentences.en: And what seems on the surface like a big deal, North Korea saying that it's going to denuclearize is actually a pretty small deal.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为朝鲜无核化确实是一件小事。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that North Korea denuclearizing is indeed a small deal.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，没什么新鲜的。

sentences.en: I mean, they've, you know, there's nothing new there.
sentences.zh: 至于军事演习，听着，如果能作为我们获得某些回报的过程的一部分，我愿意放弃它们。

sentences.en: The military exercises, you know, look, I'd be willing to give them up as part of a process in which we gain something.
sentences.zh: 但我认为我们不应该白白放弃。

sentences.en: But I don't think we should just give them up for nothing.
sentences.zh: 鉴于你刚才的解释，为什么我们认为特朗普总统会以这种方式进行谈判，为了他所得到的回报而放弃了他所放弃的东西？

sentences.en: Given what you've just explained, why do we think that President Trump negotiated the way he did, gave up what he gave for what he got in return?
sentences.zh: 我认为他是在真空中，在历史的真空中，在高层建议的真空中处理这次峰会的。

sentences.en: I think that he approached this summit in a vacuum, in a vacuum of history, in a vacuum of high-level advice.
sentences.zh: 他想抛开历史的包袱和人权的包袱，仅仅根据他与金正恩的个人感觉来达成协议。

sentences.en: He wanted to leave the baggage of history and the baggage of human rights behind and just work out a deal based on his feelings with Kim Jong-un.
sentences.zh: 那么在那种真空中运作，总统在这些谈判中必须搁置和忽视哪些历史部分和哪些问题？

sentences.en: So to operate in that kind of a vacuum, what parts of history and what kinds of issues does the president have to set aside and ignore in these negotiations?
sentences.zh: 你是我唯一做过户外采访的人，气温大约有130华氏度，但这没关系。

sentences.en: You're the only one I've done an outdoor interview, and it's about 130 degrees, but that's OK.
sentences.zh: 我想大约有150度，但不管怎样。

sentences.en: I think it's about 150, but anyway.
sentences.zh: 他接受了美国之音格蕾塔·范·萨斯特伦的采访，表现得就像是世界主要独裁者之一的发言人。

sentences.en: He gave an interview to Greta Van Susteren, a voice of America, and really kind of came across as a spokesman for one of the world's leading dictators.
sentences.zh: 今天金正恩有什么让你感到惊讶的吗？

sentences.en: What surprised you today about Kim Jong-un?
sentences.zh: 真的，他很有个性。

sentences.en: Really, he's got a great personality.
sentences.zh: 他是个有趣的人。

sentences.en: He's a, you know, funny guy.
sentences.zh: 他是个非常聪明的人。

sentences.en: He's a very smart guy.
sentences.zh: 他是个伟大的谈判者。

sentences.en: He's a great negotiator.
sentences.zh: 他爱他的人民。

sentences.en: He loves his people.
sentences.zh: 并不是说我对此感到惊讶，但他确实爱他的人民。

sentences.en: Not that I'm surprised by that, but he loves his people.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们已经开启了一项了不起的协议。

sentences.en: And I think that we have, you know, the start of an amazing deal.
sentences.zh: 他将美国军事演习描述为挑衅性的，这正是朝鲜一直以来的说法。

sentences.en: He described American military exercises as provocative, which is what North Korea has always said they are.
sentences.zh: 但我们将节省一大笔钱。

sentences.en: But we'll be saving a tremendous amount of money.
sentences.zh: 另外，我认为这非常有挑衅性。

sentences.en: Plus, I think it's very provocative.
sentences.zh: 在谈到人权时，他说，是的，朝鲜在人权方面有问题，但其他国家也有。

sentences.en: And in talking about human rights, he said, yeah, North Korea has problems with human rights, but then other countries do, too.
sentences.zh: 这很艰难。

sentences.en: It's rough.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，很多地方都很艰难。

sentences.en: It's rough in a lot of places, by the way.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统似乎更关注的不是过去，而是未来的可能性。

sentences.en: What seems to engage President Trump more is not the past, but is possibilities of the future.
sentences.zh: 地球上居住着70亿人。

sentences.en: Seven billion people inhabit planet Earth.
sentences.zh: 在今天活着的人中，只有少数人会留下持久的影响。

sentences.en: Of those alive today, only a small number will leave a lasting impact.
sentences.zh: 这次峰会最引人注目的事情之一是，他拿出一台iPad，播放了一段四分钟的宣传片，

sentences.en: And one of the remarkable things about this summit was that he pulled out an iPad and showed a four-minute promo,
sentences.zh: 一段关于朝鲜和美国未来和睦相处的可能性的四分钟预告片，

sentences.en: kind of a four-minute trailer of the possibilities of a future in which North Korea and the U.S.
sentences.zh: 还有经济发展的愿景。

sentences.en: get along.
sentences.zh: 还有经济发展。

sentences.en: And there's economic development.
sentences.zh: 还有经济发展。

sentences.en: History is always evolving.
sentences.zh: 历史总是在不断演变。

sentences.en: And there comes a time when only a few are called upon to make a difference.
sentences.zh: 总有那么一个时刻，需要少数人挺身而出，去改变现状。

sentences.en: And he tried to seduce Kim Jong-un with this vision of what might be possible.
sentences.zh: 他试图用这种愿景来诱导金正恩，让他看到未来可能的样子。

sentences.en: What if a people that share a common and rich heritage can find a common future?
sentences.zh: 如果一个拥有共同且丰富遗产的民族能够找到共同的未来，会怎样呢？

sentences.en: Their story is well known.
sentences.zh: 他们的故事众所周知。

sentences.en: But what will be their sequel?
sentences.zh: 但他们的续集会是什么样呢？

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Kind of like a trailer of the future.
sentences.zh: 就像是未来的预告片。

sentences.en: Of a movie yet to be made.
sentences.zh: 一部尚未拍摄的电影的预告片。

sentences.en: To a degree that feels unsettling, I wonder if to even enter negotiations with a dictator as brutal as Kim Jong-un,
sentences.zh: 在某种令人不安的程度上，我怀疑是否真的要与像金正恩这样残暴的独裁者进行谈判，

sentences.en: if you have to cast aside his atrocities and his repugnant behavior, even to start a negotiation with him.
sentences.zh: 如果你必须抛开他的暴行和令人反感的行为，哪怕只是为了开始与他谈判。

sentences.en: I think it's a mistake to ignore human rights, for example.
sentences.zh: 我认为忽视人权是一个错误，例如。

sentences.en: I don't think that human rights should be a condition of a nuclear deal.
sentences.zh: 我不认为人权应该成为核协议的先决条件。

sentences.en: But look, this is a country that the United Nations itself said has no parallel in the world today for violations of human rights.
sentences.zh: 但你看，这个国家连联合国自己都说，其侵犯人权的程度在当今世界是绝无仅有的。

sentences.en: It's a country where if somebody has a radio that has a dial so they can pick up a South Korean or Chinese stations,
sentences.zh: 在这个国家，如果有人拥有一台可以调频收听韩国或中国电台的收音机，

sentences.en: then not only will they be sent to a labor camp, but three generations of the entire family will be sent.
sentences.zh: 那么不仅他们会被送进劳改营，连他们的祖孙三代也会被一并送去。

sentences.en: And for the U.S.
sentences.zh: 而对于美国来说，

sentences.en: not to raise these issues and make it clear to Kim Jong-un that when you have 100,000 political prisoners in these camps,
sentences.zh: 如果不提出这些问题，并不明确地告诉金正恩，当你在这些营地里关押了十万名政治犯时，

sentences.en: that you're just not going to be accepted in the world today, you know, I think that's a missed opportunity.
sentences.zh: 你就不会被当今世界所接受，你知道，我认为这是一个错失的机会。

sentences.en: So in your mind, it's very much possible to tie this history to these negotiations, to bring them up and to make them a part of the discussions.
sentences.zh: 所以你认为，将这段历史与这些谈判挂钩，提出来并将其作为讨论的一部分，是非常可能的。

sentences.en: Look, there's always a risk in complicating any negotiation.
sentences.zh: 看，让任何谈判变得复杂总是有风险的。

sentences.en: And there are all kinds of issues that different groups think are important.
sentences.zh: 而且不同群体认为重要的议题各种各样。

sentences.en: But in 2000, for example, Madeleine Albright went to North Korea for a negotiation.
sentences.zh: 但例如在2000年，马德琳·奥尔布赖特曾前往朝鲜进行谈判。

sentences.en: I have often spoken about the importance of the World Food Program.
sentences.zh: 我经常谈到世界粮食计划署的重要性。

sentences.en: And the way she approached human rights was she brought on her delegation the assistant secretary for human rights
sentences.zh: 她处理人权问题的方式是，她在代表团中带上了负责处理人权事务的助理国务卿，

sentences.en: as part of the small group that was at the table with the North Koreans.
sentences.zh: 作为与朝鲜人坐在谈判桌前的小组的一部分。

sentences.en: But it's so important to see it in person because your work is vital.
sentences.zh: 但亲眼看到这一切非常重要，因为你们的工作至关重要。

sentences.en: Because these children and their brothers and sisters around the country should be able to grow up without fear of emergency shortages or famine.
sentences.zh: 因为这些孩子以及全国各地的兄弟姐妹们，应该能够在没有紧急短缺或饥荒恐惧的情况下成长。

sentences.en: And that was a way of signaling to the North Koreans that, look, this is an issue that the U.S.
sentences.zh: 这是一种向朝鲜人发出信号的方式，即，看，这是一个美国

sentences.en: cares about.
sentences.zh: 关心的问题。

sentences.en: And that if you want normalization of relations, then you've got to clean up your act.
sentences.zh: 而且如果你想要关系正常化，那么你就必须改过自新。

sentences.en: I wonder, in your mind, Nick, for this first meeting, which the president says is just kind of an opening salvo in these long-term negotiations with Kim Jong-un,
sentences.zh: 尼克，我想知道，在你看来，对于这次总统所说的只是与金正恩长期谈判的开场白的首轮会晤，

sentences.en: what could have been agreed to that would have been meaningful?
sentences.zh: 达成什么协议才是有意义的？

sentences.en: What would have been the agreement that you felt would be a success for the United States?
sentences.zh: 你认为什么样的协议对美国来说才算成功？

sentences.en: I think that it would have been key for North Korea to promise no more nuclear tests, no more missile tests, no more production of plutonium, no more enrichment of uranium.
sentences.zh: 我认为关键在于朝鲜承诺不再进行核试验、不再进行导弹试验、不再生产钚、不再浓缩铀。

sentences.en: So, real specific understandings about what it means to denuclearize.
sentences.zh: 所以，对于去核化意味着什么，要有真正具体的共识。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But look, I mean, I must also say that the problems of today are a lot better than the problems of six months ago.
sentences.zh: 但你看，我的意思是，我也必须说，今天的问题比六个月前的问题好多了。

sentences.en: So, I think that the Singapore summit was very badly handled.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为新加坡峰会的处理方式非常糟糕。

sentences.en: But I'm really happy that he is now engaging North Korea and that they are conducting real talks.
sentences.zh: 但我真的很高兴他现在正在与朝鲜接触，并且他们正在进行真正的会谈。

sentences.en: And, you know, I hope to be proven wrong and maybe down the road some of these things will be fleshed out.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我希望事实证明我是错的，也许在未来这些事情会变得更加充实。

sentences.en: So, despite all the objections that you have to how Trump conducted these negotiations and all the history and human rights that he seemed to disregard,
sentences.zh: 所以，尽管你对特朗普处理这些谈判的方式，以及他似乎无视的所有历史和人权问题有诸多反对意见，

sentences.en: are both countries, the United States and North Korea and our allies, now safer because Trump and Kim are engaged in these talks?
sentences.zh: 现在美国、朝鲜以及我们的盟友是否因为特朗普和金正恩参与了这些会谈而变得更安全了？

sentences.en: Does that automatically lower the chances of nuclear conflict and therefore represent a step in the right direction?
sentences.zh: 这是否会自动降低核冲突的可能性，从而代表着朝着正确方向迈出了一步？

sentences.en: Yes, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是。

sentences.en: I think that maybe the biggest single risk of the next couple of years was indeed the possibility of a nuclear war beginning in the Korean Peninsula.
sentences.zh: 我认为未来几年最大的单一风险确实是朝鲜半岛爆发核战争的可能性。

sentences.en: And I think that is not going to happen now.
sentences.zh: 而我认为现在这种情况不会发生了。

sentences.en: And that is because the psychology has been changed and there's much less risk of a military accident sparking a broader conflagration.
sentences.zh: 这是因为心理状态已经改变，军事事故引发更大规模冲突的风险大大降低了。

sentences.en: There's also much less risk that President Trump will order an attack on a missile launch in North Korea, for example.
sentences.zh: 例如，特朗普总统下令攻击朝鲜导弹发射场的风险也大大降低了。

sentences.en: So, what happened in Singapore, it's a little like that word denuclearization, full of ambiguity.
sentences.zh: 所以，新加坡发生的事情，有点像“去核化”这个词，充满了歧义。

sentences.en: What was achieved so far is not very impressive and in terms of substance is pretty disappointing.
sentences.zh: 到目前为止取得的成就并不令人印象深刻，在实质内容方面也相当令人失望。

sentences.en: One can hope, though, that this is the start of a conversation, that this is the start of a process.
sentences.zh: 不过，人们可以希望这是对话的开始，是进程的开始。

sentences.en: And it's also striking that President Trump and the Republicans have, in effect,
sentences.zh: 而且令人瞩目的是，特朗普总统和共和党人实际上，

sentences.en: embraced precisely the process of engagement that Democrats have been talking about vis-a-vis North Korea for more than 20 years.
sentences.zh: 采纳了民主党人二十多年来一直在谈论的针对朝鲜的接触政策。

sentences.en: And if there actually is bipartisan support now for engaging a rogue regime like North Korea and trying to solve these problems with diplomacy rather than with bombers,
sentences.zh: 如果现在两党真的支持与像朝鲜这样的流氓政权接触，并试图通过外交而不是轰炸机来解决这些问题，

sentences.en: we'll all be safer.
sentences.zh: 我们所有人都会更安全。

sentences.en: Nick, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 尼克，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: Good to be with you.
sentences.zh: 很高兴和你在一起。

sentences.en: I think, honestly, I think he's going to do these things.
sentences.zh: 老实说，我认为他会做这些事情。

sentences.en: I may be wrong.
sentences.zh: 我也许错了。

sentences.en: I mean, I may stand before you in six months and say, hey, I was wrong.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，六个月后我可能会站在你面前说，嘿，我错了。

sentences.en: I don't know that I'll ever admit that, but I'll find some kind of an excuse.
sentences.zh: 我不知道我是否会承认这一点，但我会找某种借口。

sentences.en: Okay, one or two, one more.
sentences.zh: 好的，一两个，再来一个。

sentences.en: Come on.
sentences.zh: 来吧。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·朗森。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《重塑者》，这是一个关于热爱设计及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you.
sentences.zh: 即使在黑胶唱片时代的夜店当DJ时，你每天晚上也要带着300件你最珍贵的宝贝去上班。

sentences.en: And you turned a DJ booth into this, like, living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你会把DJ台变成一个活生生的、充满美丽50年历史文物的快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼的《重塑者》。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁了？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to The Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 大家都知道你需要订阅《时报》才能访问所有的报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore The Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果你可以免费试用《时报》一个月，而且无需输入信用卡信息呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download The New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你第一次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在应用里的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 用一个月的时间越过付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to The New York Times, download The Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载《时报》应用程序，获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要知道的其他内容。

sentences.en: A federal judge has approved AT&T's $85 billion takeover of Time Warner,
sentences.zh: 一名联邦法官批准了AT&T以850亿美元收购时代华纳的交易，

sentences.en: rejecting the Trump administration's argument that the merger would lead to fewer choices and higher prices for consumers.
sentences.zh: 驳回了特朗普政府关于该合并将导致消费者选择减少、价格上涨的论点。

sentences.en: The ruling clears the way for the creation of a media giant that would combine the distribution systems of AT&T, a phone and internet provider, with the content of Time Warner,
sentences.zh: 这一裁决为创建一个媒体巨头扫清了障碍，该巨头将结合AT&T（一家电话和互联网提供商）的分销系统与时代华纳的内容，

sentences.en: the owner of CNN, HBO, and Warner Brothers Pictures.
sentences.zh: 时代华纳是CNN、HBO和华纳兄弟影业的所有者。

sentences.en: Something both companies said was necessary to compete with new rivals like Netflix and Amazon, which both make and distribute content.
sentences.zh: 两家公司都表示，这对于与Netflix和亚马逊等既制作又分发内容的新竞争对手竞争是必要的。

sentences.en: The Times reports that the court's decision will likely lead to similar mergers across the media industry.
sentences.zh: 《时报》报道称，法院的这一决定可能会导致整个媒体行业出现类似的合并。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 《每日新闻》到此结束。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周的《Wirecutter秀》，我们正准备迎接假期招待客人。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 收听节目，获取让客人感到宾至如归的秘诀。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是需要完全遮光才能入睡的人吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们是否会昏睡过去。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们需要什么样的光线环境？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为那是一件非常具体的事情。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症或食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们是喝咖啡还是喝茶的人？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.en: Find The Wirecutter Show on The New York Times app or wherever you like to listen.
sentences.zh: 在《纽约时报》应用程序或任何你喜欢收听的地方找到《Wirecutter秀》。
